headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGPT can write and egress while LightZero is read-only/non-runnable, so interaction risks are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content and execute shell commands, so malicious text could influence it if LightZero outputs are manually copied into its inputs. LightZero itself has no filesystem read/write or MCP surface, so there is no direct automated bridge; the pathway is unusual and manual.
conditions: IF an operator copies LightZero-generated text into AutoGPT prompts or files
IF AutoGPT is configured to treat file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep a strict manual review step before pasting any LightZero output into AutoGPT
Use a separate staging file with plain-text formatting only
Disable shell execution in AutoGPT for the session
Add a prompt prefix that treats imported text as untrusted data

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has allowlisted network egress and filesystem access, but the pair shows no shared workspace, no secrets, and LightZero cannot read files or send network traffic. That makes leakage from LightZero into AutoGPT unlikely unless an operator explicitly transfers data between them.
conditions: IF sensitive files are manually placed into AutoGPT's filesystem workspace
IF an operator exports LightZero artifacts into AutoGPT prompts or files
mitigations: Do not place sensitive data in AutoGPT's working directory
Use separate directories for the two agents
Review allowlisted egress destinations before running AutoGPT
Strip secrets from any LightZero artifacts before transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while LightZero cannot write files, modify git state, or use subprocesses. There is no overlapping write authority in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is minimal and mostly limited to operator-managed shared resources.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory by the operator
IF external tooling grants LightZero write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Avoid running both agents against the same git checkout
Lock shared files before AutoGPT writes them
Do not grant LightZero extra filesystem permissions

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs that a downstream process might consume, but LightZero is not runnable and has no action-taking or parsing surface in the profile. Without a documented pipeline from AutoGPT into LightZero, cascading error is limited to manual misuse rather than a default automated chain.
conditions: IF an operator feeds AutoGPT outputs into a LightZero workflow without verification
IF LightZero is wrapped by external automation that acts on AutoGPT text
mitigations: Require human review of AutoGPT outputs before reuse
Add a validation checklist for any downstream action
Keep LightZero isolated from AutoGPT-generated instructions
Log and diff any transferred artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, regulated data class, retention, or certification mismatch is evidenced in either profile. AutoGPT lists no touched data classes and LightZero likewise lists none, so there is no compliance pathway to assess beyond absent information.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data classes
IF a deployment policy introduces residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Add retention settings to the runbook
Review residency requirements if regulated data is introduced
